citations.review_text:
Ignore my play time, I played this fully through Uplay back in the day when it launched. I bought it a second time (deeply discounted so I could justify it) just so I could replay one of if not the last truly great Assasssin's Creed games (Valhalla is pretty good too, I don't hate it). 

The story is cool (if you ignore the very brief but very ♥♥♥♥♥♥ girlboss modern day interludes). The voice acting on Kassandra is incredible (I did not enjoy Alexios very much so my recommendation is not picking him). The world is massive, and I know that is not always a good thing, but it's just so gorgeous and I love exploring it. 

It does still have some of the infamous Ubisoft "find all the ? on the map" things but not nearly to the degree of something like AC3. The combat is certainly not revolutionary but it's engaging and enjoyable enough to keep me interested and to entice me back for a second very long playthrough. 

Ubisoft as a company blows, but this is and always will be an absolute gem.

It has some impressive visuals and a beautiful open world, but the experience becomes repetitive after a while. The huge map is filled with activities that often feel like filler, and the RPG mechanics sometimes make progression feel more like a grind than an adventure. The story has interesting moments, but the pacing suffers from the amount of side content required to move forward. A decent open-world game, but it loses some of the focused identity that made earlier Assassin’s Creed titles stand out.

**Assassin's Creed Odyssey** is one of the most impressive open-world RPGs I have ever played. From the moment I entered Ancient Greece, I was amazed by the breathtaking landscapes, beautiful islands, and vibrant cities. Every region feels unique, making exploration enjoyable from beginning to end.

One of the game's greatest strengths is its freedom. You can choose how to approach combat, whether through stealth, melee, ranged attacks, or powerful abilities. The RPG progression system allows you to experiment with different builds, and the variety of weapons and armor keeps character customization interesting throughout the adventure.

The story is also engaging, especially with the choices that affect dialogue and multiple endings. Meeting famous historical figures, sailing across the Aegean Sea, and discovering hidden ruins make the world feel alive. There is always something new to explore, whether it's a side quest, a fortress, or a mysterious cave.

Visually, the game is stunning. The lighting, weather effects, oceans, forests, and ancient architecture create one of the most beautiful worlds Ubisoft has ever built. Even after dozens of hours, I still found myself stopping just to admire the scenery.

If I had to mention a minor downside, it would be that the map is extremely large. Some side activities can become repetitive, and completing everything requires a significant time investment. However, considering the amount of content available, I think it's a reasonable trade-off.

Overall, Assassin's Creed Odyssey is an outstanding RPG filled with exploration, adventure, memorable characters, and an incredible world. If you enjoy open-world games with beautiful environments and hundreds of hours of content, I highly recommend it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game requires completing side quests and involves heavy grinding due to enemy level scaling and expensive gear upgrades.

citations.review_text:
A good game with a good story that starts off nicely. But further you go, the frustration grows:
- Level scaling is pretty bad, even one level can sometimes keep you struggling against an enemy
- Upgrading your gear costs a lot to bring it up to scale: you loot all possible locations, get all the drops, kill all the enemies, and STILL barely can upgrade your gear once, and after two or three levels it becomes obsolete again, and you need to start grinding again so you could have a chance
- The level difference for main quests sometimes jumps which obligates you to complete all the side-quests you see, not because you want to and get appealed to them, but because you NEED TO

All in all, it is a good game, for a single playthrough, because I at least do not have the patience to go through so many hours of grinding again

Assassin's Creed Odyssey isn't just one of my favorite Assassin's Creed game, it's one of the best open-world RPGs I've ever played.

From the moment the game recreates the Battle of Thermopylae, it grabs your attention and never really lets go. The journey of Kassandra is filled with memorable characters, emotional moments, and plenty of choices that make the adventure feel personal. Ancient Greece is absolutely breathtaking, with every island, city, and mountain inviting you to explore just a little bit longer.

Combat is fast, satisfying, and incredibly fun thanks to the wide variety of abilities and builds you can create. Whether you prefer charging headfirst into battle, picking enemies off with a bow, or silently clearing an entire fort without being detected, the game gives you the freedom to play your way. Recruiting defeated enemies to your ship instead of killing them is a small feature, but one that adds another layer to the experience.

Speaking of ships, naval combat is surprisingly addictive. Upgrading your vessel, assembling a unique crew, and engaging in sea battles across the Aegean Sea never stopped b…

Assassin’s Creed Odyssey is easily one of my favorite games, and after completing it about three different times, I still find reasons to come back.

Ancient Greece is one of the most beautiful and enjoyable open worlds Ubisoft has created. The map is massive, but it never feels empty. There are islands to explore, naval battles, forts to clear, mercenaries to hunt, legendary animals, side quests, and plenty of hidden locations that reward you for wandering away from the main story.

The combat is fast, satisfying, and gives you a lot of freedom in how you build your character. You can focus on stealth, direct combat, ranged attacks, or combine everything depending on the situation. The ability system and gear options make each playthrough feel different, especially once you start experimenting with specialized builds.

The story is also much more personal than I expected. Your choices can affect relationships, quests, and even the fate of your family. Some decisions are more meaningful than others, but they still make the journey feel like your own. The voice acting, especially for Kassandra, is excellent and gives the game a lot of personality.

It may not feel exactly like the older Assassin’s Creed games, but taken on its own, Odyssey is an outstanding open-world action RPG. It has a huge amount of content, memorable characters, great combat, an incredible setting, and enough replay value that I have finished it three times.

Absolutely recommended.

Also, even though it's not Deck verified it runs splendidly on it. I almost exclusively play on the Deck, and it runs between 40 and 60 FPS for the most part.

I did not finish the game so far either. If I had to guess I'm about 70% through the main game, though I didn't even touch the DLC yet.

Honestly, AC Odyssey is an incredible open-world RPG. Ancient Greece is huge, gorgeous, and full of life, and playing as Kassandra is awesome with all the naval combat and mythical gear. The reason it’s an 7/10 for me instead of higher is that the map can feel a bit overwhelming, and the heavy level-gating grinds the pacing down at times. But if you love massive RPGs and ancient history, it’s definitely a blast.

Game is good overall, took me 141hrs to complete my first playthrough in nightmare difficulty, 100% map + quests completion (Base game only, dont own dlcs). The story is exciting and revealing for the grand scheme of the saga. Compared to origins the graphic quality seemes to have dropped drastically, no idea why. Its more RPGish than origins, leaning heavily into RNG for gear stats, the world is huge and, as oposed to origins which had very deep, unique and interesting quests, odyssey's are far more generic and repetitive, of course, some of them are also fantastic. I didnt quite enjoy the "travelling downtime" on odyssey, not enough fast travel points.
Parkour is fine, fluent and responsive, but the game in general doesnt feel like an Asassins Creed, its best to think of as just a cool greek mythology RPG.
Ultimately satisfied with the game, would reccomend it to anyone who enjoys action RPGs in general and im ready to continue with valhalla!

I hate that I love this game. 
Do note that game is very very veeeeeery long even if you are jobless like me,it's gonna take you months to explore everything in the game. It's not an assassins creed but more of an adventures of a Greek mercenary as you go around exploring and helping. 
Story is quite good,mysterious with each chapter though last chapter of good ending felt a teen wrote it who got into slice of life anime genre.
Characters are best written ones I seen in an assassins creed game,Alexios/Kassandra is one of best main characters in an rpg game and side characters like Sokrates are quite memorable 
The world is quite sexy looking for a 2018 game BUT the gameplay is horrible. You are gonna need to grind levels for certain missions to progress and exploring unknown areas was just so awful. You are either gonna clear out enemy camp, hunt an alpha animal or loot chests with bad gear. That's it and the world is one of,if not biggest worlds in a game I ever seen. If you are gonna try to explore it all within days,you will burn yourself trying to uncover every corner of the map. I personally loved first 30 hours of the game,then around 60 hours I started crying how much more of this am I gonna have to do.
So exploring and grind made me feel neutral on the game,it should have been more like origins who had it perfectly paced.  Also wasn't a fan of the story outside the simulator, the main girl is simply boring with no personality unlike Desmond from previous games, honestly should have been like syndicate where you just view cutscenes for 5 minutes and get back to the simulator.

Overall fun adventure game but a bit too grindy.almost made me quit open world games for good 
Also works flawlessly on steam deck oled,60+ fps and high graphics 
8/10 for me
P.s kinda cringe ubisoft made Kassandra as canon main character,what's the point of picking a sibling then??

Finally, I got the chance to play another game from this incredible series.

Ancient Greece was absolutely beautiful. They did an amazing job recreating the world, not only visually but also historically, which is something Assassin's Creed has always been great at. Together with the soundtrack, it made exploring the world a fantastic experience.

One thing I liked much more than in Assassin's Creed Origins was the upgrade system. In Origins I often felt like I had to stop and farm materials just to upgrade my gear. Odyssey still has the ship upgrades, but I never felt forced to grind. Most of the resources came naturally while I was playing.

This was also the first Assassin's Creed where I really started to feel the repetitive gameplay. I never had any problems with my level, but after a while I got tired of doing the same tasks over and over again: kill the captain, loot a few chests, move on to the next one. Around the halfway point of the game I stopped doing those activities unless a quest sent me there.

The naval battles were fun, but after some time I lost interest in them as well. Once I had finished everything I wanted to do at sea, I mostly used fast travel instead.

The story was great from beginning to end. I met a lot of memorable characters, and I especially loved having Barnabas and Herodotos by my side. They were fantastic companions, and I really enjoyed the quests involving them.

As for the DLCs:

[b]Legacy of the First Blade[/b] had an interesting story, but the romance and everything that followed felt too forced to me. Some of the optional romances in the base game actually had much better chemistry. I understand that, they needed to connect Odyssey more closely to Origins, but I think it could have been handled better.

[b] The Fate of Atlantis[/b] was enjoyable, especially because I loved learning more about the First Civilization. However, I think it was a bit longer than it needed to be.

I already knew what happened to Kassandra because …

Overall it is a good game imo, but commonly known issue: full of repetitive chores (although i am aware it is not the worst offender in the series). I finished it FINALLY after 154 hours. It is pretty cool for a mythology nerd like me but yeah, obviously takes WAY too long to complete.

Honestly, AC Odyssey is an incredible open-world RPG. Ancient Greece is huge, gorgeous, and full of life, and playing as Kassandra is awesome with all the naval combat and mythical gear. The reason it’s an 7/10 for me instead of higher is that the map can feel a bit overwhelming, and the heavy level-gating grinds the pacing down at times. But if you love massive RPGs and ancient history, it’s definitely a blast.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe enemies as requiring many hits to defeat during combat.

citations.review_text: Ancient Greece is beautiful I could spend hours just walking around. This is one of my favorite games. Only complaint is that enemies are insanely spongey. Makes combat not difficult, but tedious.

Combat is an absolute slog, with even basic enemies needing dozens of hits to kill. This isn't even a problem with the levelling mechanics, as even enemies equal to you take forever to kill, which in turn makes the combat incredibly boring.

I wouldn't recommend it personally to anyone because of a lot of annoying things this game has- the naval is alright and the world is really beautiful but the combat is.. well it takes like a thousand hits to kill someone and i dont like that at all also the mercenary system is so damn annoying... if you want an ac game dont get this one if you want a fun experience as this game feels so grindy and time consuming its not worth it tbh just play origins it's far better
